first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and memory_31 shows signup simplification produced durable activation lift in SMB accounts. Memory_86 confirms shortened onboarding improved completion rates. Both memories target the same lever we're seeing decline. Verifying these two creates confidence in the mechanism before deployment. While memory_73 (promotional pricing) and memory_57 (referral incentives) are operationally attractive given competitive pressure, they optimize for short-term acquisition rather than sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a secondary reinforcement tactic; it works best after onboarding friction is resolved. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is strategically sound but requires resource allocation beyond a one-week experiment slot. Fixing onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline, should lift week-one engagement when paired with activation messaging downstream, and builds a durable foundation for both SMB and enterprise conversion.
